text: {"facts":[{"statement":"There are six integer variables, v1 through v6, each bounded from 0 to 5.","source_ids":["bounds","task"]},{"statement":"The constraints are q1: 4v1+3v2+3v3+2v4+5v5+3v6 ≡ 4 (mod 5); q2: 3v1+5v2+5v3+4v4+5v5+2v6 ≡ 3 (mod 7); q3: 5v1+4v2+4v3+2v4+2v5+5v6 ≡ 0 (mod 11); and q4: 4v1+5v2+2v3+2v4+2v5+2v6 ≡ 0 (mod 7).","source_ids":["q1","q2","q3","q4"]}],"open_requirements":["Find a six-integer tuple in declared variable order that satisfies all bounds and modular constraints, then return it as {\"values\":[...]}."],"tentative_options":[{"id":"enumerate","method":"Exhaustively test tuples in the bounded domain against all four congruences.","unverified_assumptions":["The bounds are inclusive, as ordinarily implied by minimum and maximum."]},{"id":"reduce_then_search","method":"Use modular arithmetic to simplify or combine the congruences, then search the remaining bounded candidates.","unverified_assumptions":["The modular reductions preserve all original constraints and aid the bounded search."]},{"id":"constraint_search","method":"Represent the bounds and congruences in a constraint solver and request a satisfying assignment.","unverified_assumptions":["A suitable solver is available and its modular constraints encode the stated congruences exactly."]}],"possible_checks":["Verify every returned value is an integer in [0,5].","Substitute the tuple into each q1–q4 expression and check its stated residue modulo its modulus."]}
